summary:
Owned units s0001–s0022 of Jinshu 80 were read in Chinese against every owned claim, hint, and person. The chapter gives one explicit age (年十三) and no birth years; those were correctly left unconverted. One-sided termini that rest on another person's death in the Jin annals are sound: Zhou Yi was killed in Yongchang 1 (AD 322), Wang Dun died in Taining 2 (AD 324), so the ox-heart visit and Dun’s praise of Xizhi are on or before those years. 元帝之過江 maps to Huai-di Yongjia 1 / AD 307 (Jinshu Yuan-di ji says 永嘉初; Tongjian dates the arrival at Jianye to month 9). Yu Liang’s western command and 亮臨薨 convert to AD 334–340 and AD 340 from Cheng-di Xianhe 9 and Xiankang 6 I/庚子, a January date that remains AD 340 in both Julian and proleptic Gregorian. The unsupported conversion is 時太尉郗鑒 → a closed AD 338–339 marriage window. Xi Jian did hold 太尉 from Xiankang 4 V to Xiankang 5 VIII, but the same anecdote in Shishuo Xin yu calls him 郗太傅, this chapter already uses 司徒導 as a later label, and published reconstructions place the match in Taining 1–2. That interval invents a start year and chooses one reading. No births were omitted from these units; Yu Liang’s death is the only death the Chinese states.
Owned units s0023–s0044 contain no births, deaths, or ages. Yin Hao’s Yangzhou letter is correctly bounded on or after AD 346 (晉穆帝永和二年 appointment/acceptance), and his northern campaign plus Yao Xiang’s victory are annal-backed to 永和八年–九年 (AD 352–353; the 山桑 rout stays in AD 353). Huan Wen’s feud is dated in that campaign context, not from later reception. Ma Midi’s own 初平三年八月 mission converts to AD 192 and is not dated from Wang Xizhi’s later quotation. Shang Ziping is only a retrospective exemplar, with empty active hints. Wang Dao’s undated invitation is a genuine uncertainty window across his Eastern Jin premiership (晉元帝建武元年 / AD 317 to 晉成帝咸康五年 / AD 339), while a narrower 丞相-title reading of 338–339 remains possible inside that window. Claim-153 is incorrect: its 351 start is a later 會稽 nianpu inference, not an annal or chapter date for 時殷浩與桓溫不協, and the same phrase is dated 352–353 on claim-171 and claim-957.
Owned units s0045–s0066 are the close of Wang Xizhi's letter to Yin Hao and the opening of his letter to the Prince of Kuaiji. They name no births, deaths, ages, or 同生 twins. Chen Sheng and Wu Guang are only a present-tense 勝廣 fear in the Hao letter and are correctly kept as retrospective reception with empty active hints. Yao and Shun appear only as 古人…堯舜 exemplars; legendary antiquity is the right qualitative placement and is not a Jin life date. The defective row is the closed AD 353–354 window on the Kuaiji letter (claim-173, claim-186, claim-210 and the p021/p024 hints). The Chinese gives 又與會稽王箋 and deictic 今, not a regnal year. One chapter-and-annals reading places that 箋 after the post-山桑 Hao letter, hence conventional 永和九年–十年 / AD 353–354 (Hao dismissed 永和十年二月). A competing chronology dates 《上會稽王笺》 to 永和八年 / AD 352, after the 許昌 setback while Hao still planned to go on, and the letter's 可欣之會 plus the named forward posts fit that earlier moment. A 353–354 interval chooses one reading and invents two exclusive endpoints. Conventional 永和八年–十年 labels correspond to AD 352–354 and need not equal the Gregorian year of every lunar month. Wang Xizhi's hint AD 353–355 then adds a further unsupported 355 endpoint: supplied context dates only the 永和九年 Lanting gathering, and 355 is the later resignation, not this letter. Academia Sinica's converter defaults to Julian before 1582; these claims are year-only conventional labels, not month-day Gregorian event dates.
Owned units s0067–s0088 are the close of Wang Xizhi’s letter to the Prince of Kuaiji and the start of the separate Xie An letter. No owned unit states a birth, death, age, era name, or reign year. Claim-192 and claim-196 correctly date Yin Hao’s and Xun Xian’s own present command—Wang still treats both as officers who can be sent back to Hefei and Guangling—by a year-precision window AD 352–354. Those endpoints are not guessed from 今/當今; they rest on the letter’s Xu–Luo supply geography and on Jin Shu 8 under Emperor Mu’s Yonghe era: Hao’s northern advance and Xun’s Huaiyin posting in Yonghe 8 (conventional AD 352), and Hao’s dismissal as a commoner in Yonghe 10 month 2 (conventional AD 354). onOrBefore 354 is required because the dismissal itself falls in AD 354; the same window also keeps the competing Jin Shu 80 reading that the letter follows Yao Xiang’s Yonghe 9 defeat. Claim-961 is the same Kuaiji letter’s retrospective citation of Wu Yuan and may share that reception date; empty hints for p027 and p030 correctly keep later reception out of living activity. Claim-211 and claim-232 stay undated, as 時東土饑荒 and the Xie An heading give no year. Claim-963 rightly classifies 尚書僕射 as retrospective heading diction: Xie An received that office in Ningkang 1 (AD 373), long after this Kuaiji-administration letter. Claim-962 is incorrect: 蹈東海 is not a date, and the 352–354 Hao-command window was copied onto a different letter about local grain transport.
Independent chronology review of Jinshu chapter 080 units s0089–s0110. ownedItems and ownedPeople are both empty, so this job has no claim rows, active-date hints, or person records to verdict. unitPeople is empty for every owned unit; named persons appearing only in neighboring context (p024 in s0080; p028–p034 in s0111–s0113; p030 in s0087) are outside this review. The owned Chinese is a continuous administrative memorial: grain-transport deadlines and year-end ratings (s0089–s0091), document flood since the writer took post (s0092–s0096), granary theft and a Yuyao shortfall (s0097–s0099), corvée desertion since wars began (s0100–s0104), and a proposal to fill artisan/clinic quotas with commuted convicts (s0105–s0110). Temporal phrases were read in Chinese and do not yield a named person's birth, death, age, or calendrical event. 歲終 in s0089 is a proposed annual audit, not a dated occurrence. 自吾到此 in s0092 and 近 in s0098 are undated relative tenure/recency. 未嘗得十日 in s0094 is an interrupted-work span. 自軍興以來…死亡叛散 in s0100 and 百工醫寺，死亡絕沒 in s0105 record unnamed population losses, not a biography death. 事起成十年、十五年 in s0105 are case durations, not inclusive ages, and 五歲刑 in s0106 is a five-year sentence, not an age. 自今/今 in s0106 and s0109 are hortatory policy time. No western year, reign-year, or month/day is present, so no conversion or westernBounds question arises. Context hints AD 353–355 on p024/p028 were not used as evidence. No omitted personal chronology is owned by this slice; findings are empty.
Owned units s0111–s0132 contain one explicit calendar date: the Lanting preface opening 永和九年，歲在癸丑，暮春之初. That date is Eastern Jin Emperor Mu’s Yonghe 9, cyclical guichou, conventionally AD 353; late spring / the third lunar month of that year remains inside AD 353 and does not cross the Gregorian New Year. Academia Sinica’s converter defaults to Julian before 1582-10-15, but a year-precision Western label is unaffected. Claims 212 and 219 correctly assign that year to Wang Xizhi’s own gathering and preface and do not invent a numbered month/day the chapter never writes. Xie An’s Kuaiji residence before office, the four eastern-land houses of Sun Chuo, Li Chong, Xu Xun and Zhi Dun, the goose-widow anecdote, and the later undated Wang anecdotes are all without a source year; empty active hints match that evidence. Peng Zu, Pan Yue and Shi Chong appear only as later reception, not as living activity, and must not feed life dates. Claim 964 omits the reception date of the Peng Zu allusion, which stands inside the dated preface: that year belongs on the retrospective event, not in hints-p036. No owned unit states a birth, death or countable age for an owned person; 殤 in 齊彭殤 is a generic short-lived child, not a named death.
Owned units s0133–s0154 are undated anecdote and reception prose except the explicit 母喪 of Wang Shu’s mother and Wang Xizhi’s qualitative 暮年 / 年在桑榆. The goose, disciple, and fan encounters, and the Yu Yi / Xi Yin / Yu Liang letters, remain undated personal attestations; Zhong Yao and Zhang Zhi appear only as later retrospective comparisons and must not feed life dates or active hints. The AD 354 chain is the defect. Chapter 80 never writes 永和十年: s0153 dates the mother’s death only as 以母喪居郡境, and s0156 says only 及述為揚州刺史. claim-387’s onOrBefore AD 354 therefore does not belong to the mother’s own event; that year is the conventional label of Wang Shu’s later Yang appointment, which this chapter leaves undated. Context rows that attach 永和十年 to s0156 are previous-model assertions, not independent evidence. 晉書穆帝紀 does date that appointment to 永和十年二月, 王述傳 adds 服闋 before it, and 東晉穆帝永和十年 is the conventional AD 354 year, but those witnesses were not cited on the death claim and must not be silently turned into a chapter-internal Gregorian endpoint or an active hint. hints-p049 AD 354 and the p049/p050 person records inherit the same unsupported year. Empty hints on p040–p048 and p050 match the owned narrative. No omitted births or numerical ages stand in the owned units; 少有名譽 is not a birth year.
Owned units s0155–s0177 centre on Wang Xizhi’s break with Wang Shu, the Yonghe 11 tomb oath, and the retired life that follows. The oath itself supplies the only day-level date: 維永和十一年三月癸卯朔，九日辛亥. That is Eastern Jin Emperor Mu, era 永和 (a repeated era name; here the Jin Mu reign, not later homonyms), year 11. 癸卯 as day 1 makes 辛亥 day 9, so the Chinese date is internally consistent. Wikipedia’s concordance maps 永和十一年 to AD 355 and 三月朔癸卯 to 30 March; those Western day numbers follow the usual pre-1582 Julian presentation (Academia Sinica’s converter, which defaults to Julian before 1582, was not successfully queried). A one- or two-day Julian/proleptic-Gregorian shift in the 350s still leaves the event in AD 355, so year-precision westernYear AD 355 is the right conventional year under the proleptic Gregorian year-bound used here. 羲之既去官 and the Xu Mai / Xie An sequel are therefore on or after AD 355, not after 355. Wang Shu’s Yangzhou appointment is undated in s0156; the same book’s 穆帝紀 (永和十年二月) dates it to Yonghe 10, conventionally AD 354. Jiankang Shilu (month 3) and Zizhi Tongjian (month 1) compete on the month only; all three stay inside AD 354, so the derived year is kept and the month conflict is not collapsed. Parents are already dead by the tomb oath (on or before AD 355); the father’s death is further fixed to Xizhi’s youth and is not given a false birth-year. Laozi and Zhou Ren appear only as authorities invoked in the oath and are dated as retrospective reception, not as living activity. No owned unit states a birth; the 年在桑榆 remark is an age colour already captured in context, not a convertible sui figure. Active hints match these personal events and do not recycle posthumous or merely cited names.
Owned units s0178–s0199 contain no birth, death, or age statements; Wang Xizhi's fifty-nine-sui death and Xie Wan's later defeat sit outside this slice. The Danyang gathering cluster (Liu Tan, Xu Xun, Wang Xizhi) is explicitly undated in the chapter and was given AD 347–349 from Liu Tan's external tenure. That reconstruction is right in outline—appointment in Yonghe 3/12, death in office before Chu Pou's Yonghe 5/12 death—but the lower Western bound is wrong: Yonghe 3/12 falls in January 348, so onOrAfter 347 allows a year before the documented start. The chapter's placement of 時劉惔為丹陽尹 after the 355 tomb-vow is a narrative order, not Liu Tan's own later activity; dating the gathering by his Danyang tenure rather than by the vow is correct. Wang's leisure, the first Xie Wan letter, the eastern return, and Xie An's planned tour are supported on or after the Yonghe 11/3 oath (AD 355) and before Xie Wan's Shengping 2/8 Yuzhou appointment (AD 358). The Yuzhou command in 358 and the 359 defeat hint match the Mu Di annals. Chao Fu, Xu You, Ji, and Qi remain legendary exempla. Lu Jia, Ban Si, and Yang Wangsun are undated in their own lives and correctly kept off active hints; their citation in the leisure letter is retrospective reception dated to that letter.
Independent review of Jinshu chapter 080 units s0200–s0221 for Wang Xizhi’s death notice, Xie Wan’s undated defeat tag, the Ningzhi–Sun En Kuaiji sequence, Xuanzhi’s early death, and Huizhi’s two Huan-staff posts. The chapter itself gives no reign year for 年五十九卒 or for 玄之早卒; those rows correctly stay undated and do not convert fifty-nine sui into a birth year. Posthumous 金紫光祿大夫 and the sons’ refusal stay retrospective and do not feed life dates. 萬不能用，果敗 is Xie Wan’s own defeat and converts, as a conventional Eastern Jin 穆帝升平三年 label, to AD 359. 孫恩之攻會稽 and 遂為孫所害 convert, as 安帝隆安三年十一月 events that remain inside AD 399 on a proleptic Gregorian new-moon table, to AD 399. Huan Wen’s 大司馬 tenure as his own office is supported as AD 363–373 from 哀帝興寧元年 to 孝武帝寧康元年. Huan Chong’s 車騎 identification is supported as bounds on or after AD 375 and on or before AD 384, preserving the 桓沖傳 寧康三年 車騎 reading against the 孝武帝紀 太元元年 車騎 appointment and the 太元九年 death while still 車騎. The defect is Wang Huizhi’s 為大司馬桓溫參軍: the chapter only places that staff post under a man already titled 大司馬. The rows copy Wen’s full tenure as a westernInterval and the hint “AD 363–373 adviser,” which states activity throughout those years rather than uncertainty about Huizhi’s own undated appointment. The parallel 車騎桓沖 post already uses bounds; the Wen post must do the same.
Owned units s0222–s0243 contain no births or ages. The only deaths are 獻之卒 (s0239) and 月餘亦卒 (s0241); both are claimed. Zuo Si, Jing Dan, and Sima Xiangru appear only as later reception and are correctly kept off life dates, with empty active hints. Dai Kui’s presence in 剡 and the night reading are source-undated. Wang Huizhi’s Palace Attendant tenure, resignation, and the 俱病篤 sentence likewise give no year. Xianzhi’s illness and death are dated from 及安薨 plus 未幾／俄而. Jin Shu Xiaowu annals place Xie An’s death on 東晉孝武帝太元十年八月丁酉, distinct from the earlier Wu 太元 era. Calendar tables equate that eighth-month day with AD 385 (Julian witness 10-12; proleptic Gregorian remains AD 385, not a New-Year-edge case). The 385–386 window for Xianzhi and the one-sided onOrAfter AD 385 bound for Huizhi’s death are therefore supported. hints-p083 is incorrect: it feeds Huizhi’s death into active-date-hints, which must stay separate from activity.
Owned units s0244–s0266 contain no omitted birth, death, or age statements for the owned people: Zhenzhi’s and Caozhi’s office lists are undated, Xianzhi’s 年數歲 is already extracted, and Xun Can and Liu Tan appear only as names in Xianzhi’s shame comparison. The Xie An visit is an undated 嘗 event whose sole justified Western endpoint is on or before AD 385, the Gregorian year of Xie An’s 太元十年八月丁酉 death under Jin Xiaowu; that one-sided bound and the empty retrospective hints are supported. The Huan Xuan Grand Commandant cluster is not: chapter 80 only says 桓玄為太尉, the annals place that self-appointment in 元興元年三月 (AD 402) and his next elevations in 元興二年 (AD 403), and an exact westernYear 402 turns an office-tenure window into a false point date.
Owned units s0267–s0288 contain one explicit age (七八歲時) and two source-date labels (太元中, 魏時), and no birth or death statements. The age is correctly kept as sui and not turned into a birth year; the childhood, Huan Wen fan, Xin'an marriage, and Gu Piqiang garden episodes are rightly left without Western years. 魏時 converts to the conventional Cao Wei span AD 220–265 for Wei Dan’s Lingyun-Hall anecdote (Xianzhi denies the story in the same passage; the claimed setting remains Wei). 太元 is Eastern Jin Xiaowu’s era, conventionally AD 376–396, not Sun Quan’s homonymous Wu era. That full-era window is not a justified uncertainty band for Xie An’s or Wang Xianzhi’s own Taiyuan events: the same chapter continues 及安薨…未幾…俄而卒於官, and Jinshu 9 dates 衛將軍、太保謝安薨 to 太元十年八月, whose conventional Western year is AD 385. claim-667, claim-674, claim-716, hints-p089, and person p089 therefore treat activity throughout Taiyuan as if both men could still act in AD 396. The on-or-before-385 hosting hint is consistent with Xie An’s death; empty hints for p090–p093 match the undated owned episodes.
The Taiyuan office and Wuxing posting rows for Wang Xianzhi (p082) convert 太元中 as AD 376–396, which is the conventional Xiaowu era label but not a possible window for these appointments: 尋除 follows the plaque talk with living Xie An and precedes 及安薨 and 俄而卒於官, so the events cannot fall after AD 385. Xie An’s death (及安薨) and Xiaowu’s same-year 殊禮 convert from 太元十年 in the 孝武帝紀 to AD 385; Xianzhi’s illness and death stay a 385–386 未幾/俄而 bound, not a single year, and the 397 追贈/諡 when 安僖皇后立 is retrospective reception (隆安元年 立皇后王氏) that must stay off active life hints. Xiaowu’s 踐阼 is 咸安二年七月 / AD 372. 先帝 is Jianwen’s conventional 咸安元年–二年 span AD 371–372; the verified November accession day already falls in AD 372, so 371 is the era label rather than a Gregorian reign day. s0347 弱冠遐棲 is an omitted traditional age for Xie An and must not become a birth year. Jingzhi’s heir-making needs onOrAfter AD 385 from the death sequence; 義興太守 and the Xi-family identifications remain undated. Legendary 箕皓, Huan Xuan’s undated collecting, and empty hints on undated kin are left as such. No births are stated in the owned units.
Owned units s0300–s0321 are the Xu Mai appendix after Wang Xizhi. The only explicit calendar label is 永和二年 on the Lin'an western-hills move (s0314). That era is Eastern Jin Emperor Mu (晉穆帝司馬聃), not Han or later homonymous 永和; 晉書穆帝紀 opens Yonghe 1 with a first-month amnesty and treats 二年 as the next annal year, and the 永和 (东晋) conversion table maps 永和二年/丙午 to conventional AD 346. The lunar year can run from early 346 into early 347, but the source gives no month or day, so the conventional year label AD 346 is the right Western form and is not a Gregorian event date. Narrative order is coherent: 未弱冠 visit to Guo Pu; Bao Jing still hidden; parents living while Mai keeps 懸霤 and returns at 朔望; 父母既終, wife née Sun sent home, then mountain wandering and 餌術涉三年 before the Yonghe 2 move; rename 玄/遠遊, farewell letter, Xizhi visits, and the letter citing 左元放 follow that move. One-sided before AD 346 bounds on the parents' lifetime/deaths and the sending-home are justified by that intervening multi-year sequence; visits and letters correctly use onOrAfter 346 rather than after 346. 未弱冠 is kept as an age-at-event and is not turned into a birth year. Chen Anshi, Mao Jiwei, and Zuo Ci are later/place-lore or Han-end citations, not living activity, and do not feed hints. s0320 says Mai's end is unknown (羽化 is later belief); no death year is present, which is correct. No owned unit states a birth. Existing claims and hints match this Chinese sequence.
Owned units s0322–s0344 are the chapter-end 贊 calligraphy critique. None of these sentences names a birth, death, age, ruler, polity, reign, or era year, so no Western year, bound, or active-date hint can be taken from them. s0322 is a general remark on later ornamental writing and names no person. The 贊 mentions 伯英, 師宜, 鐘, 王/王逸少, 獻之, 子雲, 王濛, and 徐偃 only as later comparative judgments or visual allusions. Qualitative phrases 一時, 以降, and 近出 mark sequence or recency inside that later judgment; they are not calendar endpoints and must not be converted into life years. The attestation rows correctly mark undatedSourceAttestation, and the paired event-participation rows for p118–p123 correctly use retrospective-reference / receptionType retrospective without feeding activity. p124 and p125 appear only as the paired paper-and-brush metaphor in the critique of 子雲, not as subjects of dated honor or work, so attestation-only records and empty hints are coherent. Empty active-date hints for all eight owned people match the owned evidence: later reception is preserved and is not treated as living activity. No competing calendar reading is present in these units.

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi is stated to have been thirteen sui when he called on Zhou Yi.
itemChecks.reason: s0007 says 年十三 of Wang Xizhi, the owner of this age claim. The row keeps reckoning sui and does not invent a birth year from inclusive age. No competing age figure appears in the owned units.

evidence.quote: 年十三，嘗謁周顗

itemChecks.event: Yu Liang, near death, submitted a memorial and died in Cheng-di Xiankang 6.
itemChecks.reason: s0020’s 亮臨薨 is Yu Liang’s own dying act, not a descendant commemoration. Jinshu Cheng-di ji dates the death to 咸康六年春正月庚子, the conventional Western year AD 340. The claim uses year precision rather than a day, so no Julian/Gregorian New Year shift arises; Xiankang 6 I remains AD 340 under both conventions.

evidence.quote: 亮臨薨，上疏稱羲之清貴有鑒裁

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi at thirteen sui visited Zhou Yi and was first served the ox-heart roast.
itemChecks.reason: The visit is Xizhi’s own event (年十三，嘗謁周顗; 顗先割啖羲之). Zhou Yi was killed in Yuan-di Yongchang 1 (annals: 周顗爲敦所害), so the living reception cannot postdate AD 322. onOrBefore 322 is a genuine one-sided bound; no start year was invented, and 年十三 was not turned into a birth year.

evidence.quote: 年十三，嘗謁周顗，顗察而異之
顗先割啖羲之，於是始知名

itemChecks.event: As a boy Wang Xizhi was slow of speech and not thought remarkable.
itemChecks.reason: s0006 describes childhood speech, with no reign year or era. undatedSourceAttestation is required; a guessed Western year would be improper.

evidence.quote: 羲之幼訥於言，人未之奇

itemChecks.event: In adulthood Wang Xizhi was eloquent, famed for integrity, and preeminent in clerical script.
itemChecks.reason: s0009’s 及長 is a life-stage note, not a calendar date. Leaving the attestation undated matches the Chinese.

evidence.quote: 及長，辯贍，以骨鯁稱，尤善隸書

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi was commended for integrity and judgment in Yu Liang’s deathbed memorial.
itemChecks.reason: The dated event belongs to Xizhi as the living subject of 上疏稱羲之, timed by Yu Liang’s 臨薨, not as later reception. Cheng-di Xiankang 6 I/庚子 is AD 340 at year precision. This is contemporaneous praise while Xizhi was serving, not a retrospective honor.

evidence.quote: 亮臨薨，上疏稱羲之清貴有鑒裁

itemChecks.event: Wang Dao is identified as Minister of Education only in Wang Xizhi’s kinship line.
itemChecks.reason: 司徒導之從子也 is a later office-label in a genealogy, not a dated act of Dao’s. The same chapter’s use of a highest title here shows why 司徒 must stay undated—and why 太尉 in s0014 cannot be treated as a safer date marker than this 司徒.

evidence.quote: 司徒導之從子也

itemChecks.event: Wang Zheng is attested as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing with no reign year.
itemChecks.reason: s0003 names 祖正，尚書郎 and nothing else. Owner is Wang Zheng; no Western year is licensed.

evidence.quote: 祖正，尚書郎

itemChecks.event: Wang Kuang first proposed the plan when the future Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangzi.
itemChecks.reason: 曠首創其議 is Kuang’s own counsel, dated by 元帝之過江也. Yuan-di ji says 永嘉初，用王導計，始鎮建鄴; Tongjian places the arrival at Jianye in Yongjia 1 month 9 (戊申), still the conventional Western year AD 307. The chapter gives no month, so year precision is right. This is the 307 southward transfer, not the 311 Yongjia refugee wave.

evidence.quote: 元帝之過江也，曠首創其議

itemChecks.event: Wang Kuang is named Administrator of Huainan in the genealogy without a reign year.
itemChecks.reason: 父曠，淮南太守 is an undated career label. It must not borrow AD 307 from the following crossing sentence.

evidence.quote: 父曠，淮南太守

itemChecks.event: The future Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangzi and established himself at Jianye.
itemChecks.reason: 元帝之過江也 names Yuan’s own crossing; the later title 元帝 is how the biography refers to Sima Rui and does not turn this into reception. Yongjia 1 / AD 307 is the chronicle year for 始鎮建鄴. He was not yet emperor; the event dated is the crossing, not the 317 accession.

evidence.quote: 元帝之過江也

itemChecks.event: Zhou Yi received the thirteen-sui Wang Xizhi and first offered him the ox-heart roast.
itemChecks.reason: The reception is Zhou Yi’s own act (顗察而異之; 顗先割啖羲之). He was killed in Yongchang 1, so onOrBefore AD 322 is the secure terminus. The source date 年十三 is Xizhi’s age, used only as the occasion, not converted into Zhou Yi’s lifespan.

evidence.quote: 嘗謁周顗，顗察而異之
顗先割啖羲之

itemChecks.event: Wang Dun as paternal uncle esteemed Wang Xizhi and compared him with Clerk Ruan.
itemChecks.reason: 敦嘗謂羲之曰 is Dun’s own speech. Ming-di Taining 2 VII records 王敦憤惋而死, so the conversation is on or before AD 324. sourceDate 從伯敦 is only the kinship cue; the bound is the death terminus, not an invented exact year.

evidence.quote: 深為從伯敦、導所器重
